articles.title: Asian Para Games conclude in Nagoya: India sign off with record 114 medals, finish fourth
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games with their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals as the week-long continental
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games with their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals as the week-long continental competition concluded with a closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal led the Indian contingent as flag-bearers at the ceremony, marking the end of a landmark campaign in which the country's para-athletes delivered historic victories, world-record performances and podium sweeps across disciplines.India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.Held in Japan for the first time, the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games brought together around 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. The competition featured 18 sports, with more than 20 world records reportedly set during the seven-day event.ALSO READ: India script history with best-ever fourth-place finishIndia finish fourth as China lead medal standingsChina topped the medal table with 435 medals, including 207 gold, while hosts Japan finished second with 186 medals — 64 gold, 60 silver and 62 bronze. Uzbekistan emerged as the third-ranked nation, collecting 145 medals, including 45 gold.India's fourth-place finish was particularly significant given the size of its contingent. A total of 168 para-athletes represented the country at Aichi-Nagoya, compared with 309 at the previous edition in Hangzhou.President Droupadi Murmu congratulated the Indian contingent on its record performance, saying the achievement reflected the athletes' hard work, perseverance and self-belief.In a post on X, Murmu said the unprecedented medal haul would inspire young people to dream big, work with dedication and remain positive in the face of challenges. She also extended her congratulations to the entire Indian contingent.Para athletics leads India's medal chargePara athletics was India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. Para badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze.India also won 11 medals in para swimming, seven in para table tennis, six in para archery and five in para shooting. The contingent added two medals each in para judo and para powerlifting.Doha to host next edition in 2030The closing ceremony brought together athletes, officials and dignitaries to mark the conclusion of the Games. Asian Paralympic Committee president Majid Rashed declared the event closed, highlighting the growing strength of para sport across Asia and its role in building a more inclusive society.Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also praised the athletes' determination, teamwork and sportsmanship, describing their performances as a reminder of the “profound beauty” of para sports.The Asian Para Games began in Guangzhou, China, in 2010, evolving from the Far East and South Pacific Games Federation for the Disabled. The Aichi-Nagoya edition was the fifth staging of the event, with Doha, Qatar, scheduled to host the sixth in 2030.For India, the closing ceremony marked the end of a historic campaign — one that raised the country's medal benchmark and showcased the depth and growing strength of its para-sport movement.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Navdeep Singh credits SAI JLN Stadium support as India deliver record Asian Para Games medal haul
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian para-javelin star Navdeep Singh has credited the support and training facilities at the Sports Authority of India’s (SAI) Jawaharlal
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian para-javelin star Navdeep Singh has credited the support and training facilities at the Sports Authority of India’s (SAI) Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) Stadium in New Delhi for helping the country’s para-athletes deliver a historic performance at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games.India finished fourth in the continental competition with a record 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — its best-ever haul at the Games. Para athletics led the charge with 65 medals, including 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze.Navdeep won bronze in the men’s javelin throw F40/F41 on Friday, improving on his fourth-place finish at the 2022 edition. The Paris Paralympics gold medallist said training alongside fellow athletes at the JLN Stadium’s main track helped him prepare for the competition environment in Aichi-Nagoya.“Most of us Asian Games-bound athletes, including me, did our preparations at the JLN Stadium for the Asian Games 2026,” said Navdeep after his medal win. “This allowed us to acclimatise and get the feel. Despite the ongoing [Indian Super League] football matches, they kept the Asian Games a priority, which I felt was quite impressive, and that supported me,” he added.Dedicated training access helped athletesNavdeep also highlighted how access to the main track allowed athletes across disciplines to focus on their preparations without unnecessary delays.“Sprinters need an empty track, so they got a good chance to train inside it. I majorly train at the SAI Regional Centres [Bengaluru, Sonipat and Gandhinagar], where there is not much crowd and I don’t have to wait for other athletes to finish their throws. This all happened here at the JLN Stadium too. I could focus on my preparations rather than focusing on rotations and waiting for my turn,” Navdeep said, expressing hopes of returning to the JLN Stadium for the next season.A total of 14 para-athletics medallists from the Aichi-Nagoya Games trained at the JLN Stadium ahead of the competition. More than 50 other para-athletes also train at the facility.JLN-trained athletes contribute to medal haulThe athletes who trained at the facility delivered medals across track and field events. Gold medallists included Praveen Kumar in the men’s high jump T64, Sandeep Kumar in the men’s 400m T64, where he set a world record, Pranav Soorma in the men’s club throw F51, Rinku Hooda in the men’s javelin throw F46, and Simran Sharma, who won the women’s 100m and 200m T12 titles, setting Games records in both events.The silver medallists included Manjeet, Nimisha Chakkungalparambil, Varun Singh Bhati, Preeti Pal and Ajeet Singh Yadav. Bronze medallists included Sandeep Kumar in the men’s 100m T44, Sandip Sanjay Sargar in the men’s javelin combined classification event, Navdeep in the men’s javelin F40/F41 and Anubhav Choudhary in the men’s 100m T35.The medal-winning performances highlighted the contribution of the JLN Stadium’s training environment to India’s record campaign at the Asian Para Games.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Michigan stuns Western Michigan again as Wolverines hockey nets winner with 0.1 seconds left
articles.summary: Will Horcoff, who was in attendance for the controversial football ending, netted the late winner.
articles.body:
An unforgettable football game 48 days ago saw the Broncos lose to Michigan on a controversial touchdown as time expired . On Friday night, the Wolverines hockey team handed WMU a similar ending, though this time with less debate about the clock.

Michigan scored three third-period goals during a 3-2 win over the fifth-ranked WMU, which ended with Will Horcoff, who was at Michigan Stadium when Bryce Underwood found JJ Buchanan last month, beating goaltender Quentin Miller with 0.1 seconds to play.

The Broncos tried a Hail Mary of their own, challenging for offside, but the goal stood.

"I honestly just went black," said Horcoff afterward via MLive.com . "I was in shock. I couldn't believe it."

"I was like, 'There's no way that actually happened,'" said defenseman Dakoda Rhéaume-Mullen. "That's a crazy coincidence. That's a crazy finish. Playing a good team like Western Michigan and winning like that at the last second, that's why you play till the last second."

The top-ranked Wolverines improved to 7-0-0 on the season and are back on the ice next weekend for two games at Ohio State.

articles.title: Josh Hoover injury update: Indiana QB playing through hurt arm suffered vs Ohio State
articles.summary: Josh Hoover is reportedly playing through an injury against Michigan on Saturday, Oct. 24.
articles.body:
Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover is on the field for pregame warmups against Michigan on Saturday, Oct. 24, despite suffering an apparent injury in Week 7's loss to Ohio State.

The first-year transfer from TCU played through the injury late in the 19-15 loss, as he appeared to aggravate something on his right throwing arm. ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Saturday that Hoover is playing through an arm and wrist issue.

Hoover has been one of the best quarterbacks in college football this season, with 1,660 passing yards and 19 total touchdowns to no interceptions. He ranks No. 2 nationally with a 89.0 QBR while completing 63.9% of his passes and 9.8 yards per attempt.

The fourth-year starter was 20-of-40 passing for 296 yards with a touchdown against the Buckeyes in Week 7, and nearly threw a game-winning touchdown in the final moments, although Nick Marsh wasn't able to stay in bounds on the catch.

Here's what to know of Hoover's injury and Indiana 's quarterback situation against the Wolverines on Saturday:

Hoover is playing through an arm/wrist injury against Michigan, Thamel reported during ESPN's "College GameDay" on Saturday.

Hoover was clearly bothered by the apparent injury in Week 7 against Ohio State, suffering the ailment in the second half of the game. Hoover was taken off the field for several plays after suffering the injury against the Buckeyes before returning.

Indiana's backup quarterback is Grant Wilson, a sixth-year senior transfer from Old Dominion. Wilson has 2,828 career passing yards with 25 touchdowns to 11 interceptions and started his career at Fordham.

Wilson passed for 2,149 yards with 17 touchdowns to eight interceptions as ODU's starter in 2023 but lost the job to now-Wisconsin starter Colton Joseph in 2024 before transferring to Indiana for the 2025 and 2026 season. The Hoosiers also have sophomore Tyler Cherry, who has played this season.

Wilson has 74 passing yards and two touchdowns this season behind Hoover.

The Pittsburgh Steelers will debut a never-before-worn uniform combination for their game in Paris on Sunday, the team announced 24 hours before the game against the New Orleans Saints.

The Steelers will be pairing their traditional white road uniform tops wth the black pants with a thick gold stripe that the team usually wears as part of its color rush jerseys.

While many NFL teams routinely mix and match their different uniform combinations, this is a first for the Steelers, who wear the same gold pants with their home and road uniforms. They wear khaki-colored pants for their vertically striped throwback uniforms.

articles.title: 'Not too high, not too low.' Danville stays perfect with sectional win over Lebanon
articles.summary: Danville improved to 10-0 after a 42-13 victory over Lebanon in the first round of the 4A Sectional 21 playoffs.
articles.body:
LEBANON −In a lopsided affair, Danville rolled past Lebanon, 42-13, in an IHSAA 4A Sectional 21 playoff game on Friday, Oct. 23.

Danville worked hard all week behind the scene.

"The key to winning was our week of preparation and practice and taking everything from the film room to the field and stacking good days of practice," said senior quarterback Carter Ward, who threw a 5-yard touchdown pass to give Danville a 34-6 lead in the third quarter and had a rushing touchdown. A great week of practice will lead to a good game. I would definitely say our preparation and our execution along with every guy knowing they are going to do their job on every single play led to us winning."

See Lebanon play Danville in IHSAA football sectional action

Ward commanded the offense, leading a run-heavy attack that totaled 242 yards on the ground. Senior running back Daiton Hood rushed for 113 yards on 19 carries and had a touchdown, and Ward had 49 yards on seven carries.

Danville (10-0) anticipated a hot Lebanon defense − which had yielded just 21 points combined in its past two games − and took advantage of any mistake they it could find.

"We knew they were going to bring some heat on defense, and we knew they were going to be ready after last time," Ward said. "Our motto was to just out-physical them, so that was our thing throughout the week. We had to come into tonight's game and out-physical them and absolutely execute and just play smarter than them."

Despite going into halftime leading, 28-6, Danville knew it could not let up.

"At halftime, we knew we just had to keep our composure," Ward said. "We like to always say 'not too high, not too low,' so just always staying right in the middle. There is a lot that can happen in the second half so we had to keep doing our thing, everybody has to do their job and execute on every single play."

Lebanon (4-6) prepared as much as it could, despite what the scoreboard said.

"Throughout the week, we watched a lot of film and looked at how we played them earlier in the season," said sophomore quarterback Jake Linton, referring to Danville's 28-14 victory on Sept. 18. "We really focused down on what they were going to do in coverage and defense as a whole. However, they switched it midway through the game, and we really tried to address our game plan and just focus down on execute the way we can."

Giving up was never an option on Lebanon's game plan.

"If you take a look at our season, we have honestly been down a bit. In the locker room, we were really confident because we knew we always are able to fight back and we have never really gave up," said Linton, who was 22-of-37 passing for 253 yards and a touchdown.

After a tough loss against Danville and the looming graduation plus the loss of many senior teammates, Linton is looking to use this year as motivation to pursue higher tournament rounds next season year .

"I know I just really need to work on my flaws." Linton said. "I know how hard I need to work to pursue bigger games next year.

Danville advances to play Brebeuf Jesuit (6-4) in the second round of the playoffs on Friday, Oct. 30.

articles.title: Pakistan squad for Sri Lanka Test series 2026: Full team lists for PAK vs SL home red-ball series
articles.summary: With a home Test series waiting for Pakistan once the ongoing tri-series with England and Sri Lanka wraps up, here's a look at their squad for the longest fo...
articles.body:
Salman Ali Agha and Ali Usman return to the Pakistan Test squad after being sent home from England .

Mohammad Taha, Mohammad Suleman and Sameer Minhas have earned their maiden call-ups for the Sri Lanka series.

Babar Azam stays on as captain, with no place for Mohammad Rizwan or Imam-ul-Haq.

Salman Ali Agha returns as two of the seven sent home from England come back to Pakistan Test squad

Pakistan have named a 14-member squad for the two-match home series against Sri Lanka, and the most notable names on it are the two players who were put on a plane home in the middle of the England tour in August.

Salman Ali Agha and Ali Usman are both back. Seven players were released from that touring party after the Lord's defeat, and only those two have found their way into this squad, with Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad all left out.

Salman's return is the sharper story of the two. He had captained Pakistan in the first Test of that series in Babar Azam's absence, was the twelfth man in the second, and was then removed from the squad entirely, with reports at the time saying he had been asked to appear before a committee over conduct on the West Indies and England tours.

Rizwan's absence has a separate explanation. He has been under inquiry by Pakistan's National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency since his phone was seized in London on the night the Lord's Test finished, and that matter remains unresolved.

Three uncapped players named in Pakistan's Test squad for Sri Lanka

Mohammad Taha, Mohammad Suleman and Sameer Minhas have all received their first Test call-ups, and all three have come through on runs scored this season rather than on reputation.

Taha, a 26-year-old left-hander, leads the President's Trophy Grade-I run charts with 730 from seven matches, including three hundred and a best of 225. Suleman sits fifth on 652, also with three centuries, while Sameer has 405 in seven games in what is only his first first-class season after coming through the Under-19 setup.

Four of the players drafted in for the final Test at Edgbaston have kept their places, with Abdullah Fazal, Arafat Minhas, Razaullah and Saad Baig all retained. Two more fast bowlers will join once the PCB Patron's XI finish their three-day game against the tourists.

Rawalpindi hosts the first Test from November 9 to 13, with the second at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium from November 17 to 21.

Pakistan have quietly walked back half of the purge they made in September

Sending seven players home mid-tour was presented as a line in the sand, and it came alongside a coaching change and seven replacements, five of them uncapped. Two months on, two of those seven are back, and the squad otherwise looks much like the one assembled in a hurry for Edgbaston.

That is not necessarily wrong. Salman Ali Agha captained the side in that series and has led Pakistan across formats, and a squad containing three debutants and very little Test batting experience needs someone who has been there. Discarding him permanently over an August decision would have been an overcorrection.

The problem is what it says about the original call. If Salman is selectable in November, the question of why he was sent home in September was never really answered, and the board has now created a situation where the men left out look punished and the ones brought back look forgiven, with nothing explained.

The squad itself is the other worry. Fourteen names and one frontline seamer in Mohammad Abbas, with two quicks to be added after a warm-up game finishes, do not make for the look of a settled plan. Pakistan are picking in-form domestic batters and working out the attack later, which can work on Rawalpindi and Lahore surfaces, but it is a thin way to start a home season.

articles.title: Baker Mayfield returns to a major challenge for Buccaneers
articles.summary: Baker Mayfield is expected to return against Carolina, but the Buccaneers' offensive line, injuries and inconsistent offense remain major concerns.
articles.body:
Baker Mayfield is expected to return to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' starting lineup Sunday against the Carolina Panthers , but the problems that plagued the offense before his injury haven't disappeared.

According to the Buccaneers' official team update , head coach Todd Bowles indicated Friday that Mayfield is ready to return after missing three games with a dislocated right thumb. The veteran quarterback participated fully in all three practices this week and has been working with a protective glove on his throwing hand. Mayfield remains officially listed as questionable.

His expected return comes at an important time for Tampa Bay, which enters Sunday's NFC South matchup at 1-5 following a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. However, expecting Mayfield to immediately fix an offense that has struggled all season overlooks several significant issues.

The Buccaneers rank 24th in total offense, averaging 292.7 yards per game, and 25th in scoring at 19.8 points per contest. They've also struggled to protect their quarterbacks, ranking 30th in sacks allowed per pass attempt at 11.34%, according to the team's official Week 7 preview .

Those problems were evident before Mayfield suffered his injury against Minnesota in Week 3.

In his first three appearances, Mayfield completed 63.5% of his passes for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions, finishing with an 80.0 passer rating. He also threw 13 interceptions, averaging more than four sacks per game. Tampa Bay lost all three contests, and the offense had already struggled to sustain drives and produce consistently.

Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels stepped into a difficult situation and helped the Buccaneers earn their first victory against Dallas. Daniels has completed 61.2% of his passes for 501 yards, three touchdowns and five interceptions across four appearances, including his relief appearance against Minnesota.

The difference between Tampa Bay's last two games illustrates how much the supporting cast matters. Against Dallas, the Buccaneers rushed for 241 yards and allowed just one sack in a 24-16 victory. A week later against Pittsburgh, Bucky Irving managed only 46 yards on 19 carries while Daniels was sacked five times in an overtime loss.

Mayfield brings experience Daniels hasn't had a chance to develop. His ability to identify pressure, adjust protections, and make pre-snap decisions should help offensive coordinator Zac Robinson run a more complete offense. However, those advantages won't matter nearly as much if Tampa Bay continues allowing defenders into the backfield.

Mayfield also won't have all of his offensive starters available. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka has been ruled out with concussion and foot injuries, while starting right tackle Luke Goedeke will miss Sunday's game with a calf injury. Egbuka leads the Buccaneers with 28 receptions for 240 yards, and his absence removes one of the team's most frequently targeted receivers.

Goedeke's absence is particularly concerning with Mayfield returning from an injury to his throwing hand. The Buccaneers cannot afford to put their quarterback in situations where he's repeatedly forced to escape pressure or absorb unnecessary hits.

Fortunately, Carolina's defense offers Tampa Bay opportunities to improve. The Panthers rank 25th in total defense, allowing 354.2 yards per game, and 27th against the run, allowing 132.2 yards per game. Carolina will also be without outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips and Thomas Incoom, who were ruled out Friday.

That should put additional emphasis on Irving and Tampa Bay's running game. The Buccaneers rank eighth in rushing offense at 127.8 yards per game, and Irving has accumulated 452 rushing yards through six games. Establishing the run could help limit obvious passing situations while giving Mayfield opportunities to work off play-action.

Robinson also needs to make adjustments; Mayfield's return should give the offensive coordinator more flexibility, but Tampa Bay still needs to create favorable matchups, protect its quarterback, and get the ball to its playmakers.

The Buccaneers rank 28th in red-zone touchdown percentage at 47.4%, another area where better execution and play-calling could make a significant difference. Moving the football means little if promising drives consistently end without touchdowns.

Tampa Bay's defense has done enough to keep the team competitive in several games this season. The offense needs to provide more support, particularly when the Buccaneers have opportunities to protect leads and control the clock.

Mayfield's expected return gives Tampa Bay a better chance to compete with the division-leading Panthers, but the Buccaneers struggled offensively before he went down. Those issues will take more than a quarterback change to fix.

Sunday will be an important test for Mayfield, Robinson, and an offense that needs to improve meaningfully before Tampa Bay falls any further behind in the NFC South.

articles.title: Philippe sinks his parent club as Paderborn end HSV's streak
articles.summary: Paderborn eased their relegation woes by ending Hamburger SV's three-game winning streak with a goal from the player they loaned from their guests.Stuttgart...
articles.body:
Paderborn eased their relegation woes by ending Hamburger SV's three-game winning streak with a goal from the player they loaned from their guests.

Stuttgart loanee Laurin Ulrich had the first chance of the game inside two minutes. The visitors failed to clear Raphael Obermaier's free-kick, and the Germany U21 international nearly scored from 18 meters.

HSV then dealt a blow as Fabio Vieira had to be substituted off for what seemed like a hamstring injury. The youngster Otto Stange replaced the Portuguese midfielder, who is yet to produce a direct goal contribution since joining the club on a permanent transfer.

There were no clear-cut chances at either side during the first-half, which was changed two minutes after the restart. Half-time substitute Tom Baack created a big chance for Santiago Castaneda, but the US midfielder was denied by a fantastic reflex save from Daniel Heuer Fernandes.

However, there was little in the way of scoring opportunities after that until the final 20 minutes. HSV's goalkeeper made a couple of saves from Obermaier and Castaneda before Laurin Curda hit the outside of the post.

The visitors had a very lackluster performance in the final third, and they threw away their point two minutes before the end of regular time. As fate has it, HSV loanee Rayan Philippe scored the only goal of the game with a composed finish against his parent club. The 26-year-old scored his first goal for his new club a day after celebrating his birthday.

HSV protested there was a foul in the buildup, but their voices only led to a yellow card for Merlin Polzin. Paderborn are now out of the relegation zone as they get past their next opponents in the cup, Stuttgart. The traditional club will face Eintracht Frankfurt in the second round of the DFB-Pokal.

articles.title: Leipzig return to winning ways, Füllkrug brace in Bremen win
articles.summary: Christoph Baumgartner scored on his Bundesliga return as RB Leipzig rebounded from two heavy defeats with a 4-0 victory over Elversberg on Saturday while in-...
articles.body:
Christoph Baumgartner scored on his Bundesliga return as RB Leipzig rebounded from two heavy defeats with a 4-0 victory over Elversberg on Saturday while in-form Niclas Füllkrug added another brace in Werder Bremen's 3-2 in Mainz.

Leipzig and their new coach Martín Demichelis were under pressure to deliver after a 6-1 defeat at Bayern Munich and a 4-1 loss at Real Madrid.

They responded against promoted Elversberg as Tidiam Gomis converted a pass from Antonio Nusa in the 48th minute and Nusa then also set up Rômulo for the second in the 66th with a long ball.

Baumgartner came on for his first league match of the season after a thigh injury that cost him playing for Austria at the World Cup, and showed his worth with a thumping header in the 84th before Rômulo wrapped up matters.

Leipzig moved past Elversberg and Mainz into fifth, ahead of Bremen on goal difference.

Füllkrug became the first Bremen player since club and Germany legend Rudi Völler 41 years ago to reach eight goals in seven matches when he converted penalties in the seventh and 25th minute.

Hosts Mainz revived their hopes from Anthony Caci's header in the 33rd. Bremen got a third from a deflected shot by Ludovit Reis in the 61st, Lee Jaesung responded with a glancing header two minutes later but Bremen held on.

Elsewhere, Cologne and Schalke drew 0-0 while SV Hamburg's run of three straight victories ended with a 1-0 at Paderborn, with on-loan Rayan Philippe condemning his parent club to defeat in the 88th.

Augsburg and Union Berlin drew 1-1 from a 71st-minute diving header by Han-Noah Massengo for the hosts and Janik Haberer's equalizer three minutes later. Union had Felix Uduokhai sent off against his former club for a last-man foul, and Augsburg's Juma Bah followed for a reckless tackle.

Borussia Dortmund host Eintracht Frankfurt in the late game and will go top if they don't lose. They are tied on points with champions Bayern Munich and one point ahead of Freiburg and Bayer Leverkusen.

Bayern visit Freiburg on Sunday without coach Vincent Kompany, who is in hospital after collapsing on Friday, goalkeeper Manuel Neuer and winger Luis Díaz. Leverkusen play the other Sunday game at Hoffenheim.

Borussia Mönchengladbach won 3-2 at VfB Stuttgart on Friday to claim their first points of the season on the seventh attempt.

articles.title: Natalia Granada reveals the family influence behind her racing passion as she takes on her first F1 Academy season
articles.summary: Natalia Granada’s first F1 Academy season has brought a major step forward in her racing career, but her path to single-seaters began with family Formula
articles.body: Natalia Granada’s first F1 Academy season has brought a major step forward in her racing career, but her path to single-seaters began with family Formula 1 evenings and a question about Fernando Alonso. The 18-year-old Spaniard and her twin brother, Marc, grew up watching races with their parents before discovering that go-karting was Alonso’s route into the sport. Now racing full-time in the all-women’s series, Granada is learning to manage competition, education and life away from the track. With support from the Iron Dames, she is also preparing for the next stage of her career.Natalia Granada’s racing journey began with her family’s love for F1Granada’s interest in racing grew from a family hobby into a serious pursuit. Her parents had followed Formula 1 for years, and their enthusiasm gave the twins an early connection to the sport. The turning point came when Marc asked their father how Alonso had reached the top level of racing.“My parents were both F1 fans since forever,” Granada, 18, tells PEOPLE. “And I remember this moment, when my brother one day asked my dad, ‘How did Fernando Alonso, a very known Spanish F1 driver, start? How did he get to Formula 1?’ And so we started investigating.”The answer led them to go-karting. With a track only six minutes from their home in La Garriga, Spain, Granada had a practical way to test her interest rather than simply watch the sport from the sidelines.“From there, we just figured out the closest track,” Granada laughs. “I went there and started driving, and from there just one thing led to the next, and here we are.”That early start has now brought her to F1 Academy, where she is one of 15 full-time drivers. The series gives young women a platform to move from karting into single-seater racing, an important step for those hoping to progress through the motorsport ladder.Granada has described her debut campaign as a major learning opportunity, both on and off the circuit. “It’s been amazing,” Granada says. “It’s just been such a big opportunity to make the jump from go-karts to single-seaters. It’s such a big step in my career, such a big opportunity in every aspect racing-wise, visibility-wise, for my future. I just think it’s been one of the best platforms so far for me to keep developing in my racing and my career.”Iron Dames support and life away from racing are shaping her progressThe demands of a racing season extend beyond race weekends. Granada must balance her education with training, travel and the pressure of competing against drivers who share the same ambition to reach the highest levels of motorsport.“Online school has helped me a lot to balance everything around my tight schedule,” Granada says.She also makes room for activities that have little to do with lap times. Cooking is one of her favourite ways to unwind, with paella and sushi among her preferred dishes. Returning home to spend time with family and friends gives her a break from the demands of racing.That balance is especially important as she gains experience in single-seaters. Granada finished fourth at the Zandvoort round in the Netherlands, narrowly missing the podium. The result offered a sign of her progress during a season in which she has had to adjust to a new level of competition.The Iron Dames, a women-focused racing organisation that has helped women enter motorsport since 2019, have also played a key role in her development. Granada credits the group with providing valuable support at a young age and hopes to follow its members into higher levels of competition.“This year, I’m working more based on how I’m feeling and what I’ve learned over the past years, and I’m managing quite well,” Granada reflects. “We always say in racing, you want to be very prepared for what you’re racing now and be ready to make the next step.”With the United States rounds in Austin and Las Vegas set to close the season, Granada’s focus remains on learning and improving. Her first F1 Academy campaign is not just about where she finishes in the standings. It is also about turning the lessons from her debut year into a stronger foundation for what comes next.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Gymnastics World Championships: Great Britain's Jake Jarman wins men's floor silver medal
articles.summary: Britain's Jake Jarman wins a historic fourth World Artistic Gymnastics Championships medal, with floor silver in Rotterdam.
articles.body:
Defending world champion Jake Jarman narrowly missed out on floor gold but still became Britain's most decorated athlete in World Artistic Gymnastics Championships history.

The 24-year-old finished second to American Frederick Richard, who won his first world title by a margin of 0.333 points.

Jarman, who was the final competitor in the final in Rotterdam, recorded a score of 14.600 to secure his fourth World Championships medal, having won vault gold in 2023 and team bronze in 2022.

"I can't be annoyed although it's not the result I was aiming for," he said.

"To know that I could do a bit better yet I've still walked away with a world silver gives me a lot of confidence, and there's room for improvement, so overall I'm really happy.

"We all really pushed each other and its good fun to be a part of and I'm excited for more battles in the future."

Compatriot Courtney Tulloch, 31, was also the final competitor in the men's rings final, where a stumble on landing his dismount cost marks as he finished seventh with a score of 13.366.

Meanwhile, British 18-year-old Abi Martin, competing in her first world women's vault final, finished eighth with an average of 13.716 points from her two attempts.

Brazil's most decorated Olympian, Rebeca Andrade, took gold in the vault, in her first World Championships after taking a 22-month break from the sport.

The 27-year-old won four medals at the 2024 Paris Olympics, extending her total count to six, and then stepped away from gymnastics to focus on her mental and physical well-being.

She won her third world vault title in the presence of legendary US athlete Simone Biles, who joined the spectators in the Ahoy Arena and is yet to confirm if she will return to gymnastics after last competing in Paris.

Algerian Kaylia Nemour, the 19-year-old defending world and Olympic champion, took gold in the uneven bars, while American Skye Bradley complemented gold in Saturday's all-round final with bronze in both of the day's women's events.

Jarman will compete again on Sunday's final day of competition, alongside team-mate Hepworth in the men's vault, while Martin and Alice Kinsella will feature in the women's floor.

You can watch coverage of the Gymnastics World Championships, which run until Sunday, 25 October, on BBC Two and BBC iPlayer.

articles.title: Crisis en el Junior: la insólita marcha fúnebre y protesta con la que exigen la salida de ocho jugadores
articles.standfirst: Hinchas piden la salida de 8 jugadores con marcha fúnebre y humo negro
articles.summary: Hinchas piden la salida de 8 jugadores con marcha fúnebre y humo negro
articles.body: La crisis deportiva del Junior de Barranquilla ha llegado a un punto de ebullición insostenible para su afición. En medio de un ambiente de profunda frustración tras la eliminación anticipada del equipo de la lucha por los cuadrangulares semifinales de la Liga Colombiana, la hinchada rojiblanca protagonizó una de las manifestaciones de rechazo más inusuales y llamativas de los últimos tiempos en el fútbol profesional colombiano. Los seguidores del ‘Tiburón’ decidieron expresar su descontento de una manera gráfica y simbólica durante el compromiso frente a Águilas Doradas. Las inmediaciones del escenario deportivo se convirtieron en el escenario de una marcha fúnebre, acompañada de densas columnas de humo negro que presagiaban el luto de una temporada para el olvido. El momento cumbre de la protesta ocurrió cuando los aficionados desplegaron un gran trapo o cartel con los rostros de ocho jugadores de la plantilla actual, señalados directamente como los principales responsables del pobre rendimiento deportivo del equipo y exigiendo su salida inmediata de la institución. Las imágenes no tardaron en viralizarse a través de las redes sociales, evidenciando el tamaño de la brecha que hoy existe entre la fanaticada y los futbolistas. Las causas de esta severa crisis se hunden en la irregularidad que persiguió al Junior a lo largo del campeonato. Ni siquiera la llegada de íconos de la institución al banquillo técnico —como el nombramiento de Sebastián Viera en la dirección técnica a partir de septiembre— logró enderezar el rumbo ni encarrilar al equipo hacia la regularidad que exigía la historia del club. Los resultados adversos acumularon la presión sobre los hombros de un plantel que no supo responder a la exigencia de la hinchada barranquillera, acostumbrada históricamente a pelear por los títulos y a ser protagonista de primera línea en el rentado nacional. Ante la intensidad de los reclamos, los directivos del club sostuvieron encuentros con representantes de la hinchada para mitigar la tensión, reforzando los protocolos de seguridad. Si bien la institución ha defendido el derecho legítimo de los aficionados a manifestar su inconformismo, también ha hecho un llamado enfático a evitar los actos de violencia o intimidación. Mientras en la cancha el Junior intenta cerrar decorosamente el calendario del torneo, en los despachos y en la tribuna el verdadero partido ya comenzó: la urgente necesidad de planificar una profunda reestructuración que limpie la casa, sane la confianza y devuelva la ilusión a una de las hinchadas más apasionadas del país.

articles.title: España asegura el triunfo en el Mundial de pelota por delante de Euskadi
articles.standfirst: El equipo español suma seis oros y aspira a tres más
articles.summary: El equipo español suma seis oros y aspira a tres más
articles.body: La selección de España se aseguró el título por equipos en la última jornada de los XX Mundiales de Pelota Vasca en Buenos Aires y a falta de tres finales con competidores españoles involucrados. De momento, España suma seis oros, siete platas y un bronce, mientras que la selección de Euskadi, comunidad autónoma española que en este Mundial actúa como equipo independiente, tiene cuatro oros, cinco platas y un bronce. Aunque el equipo vasco podría sumar dos medallas doradas más, no podrá igualar la cantidad de platas con las que cuenta el combinado español. De esta forma, la delegación española será consagrada campeona en unos Mundiales que contaron con la novedad de la primera participación de la selección vasca por separado. Por supuesto, en la selección española hay jugadores vascos. La certeza del título colectivo llegó con los resultados de frontón de la mañana, cuando México se alzó con los primeros puestos masculino y femenino por encima de los dos equipos ibéricos, lo que volvió irremontable para Euskadi la gran diferencia que España había logrado en la jornada de viernes, cuando consiguió cinco oros. Resta el duelo entre España y Euskadi en pala corta masculina, en su último enfrentamiento directo de los Mundiales. Los jugadores de la Federación Española de Pelota disputarán otras dos finales, en ambos casos ante Argentina, la de paleta cuero masculina y la de paleta goma femenina. España venció a Euskadi en tres de las cuatro finales que disputaron el viernes. Ganó las de mano individual, paleta goma y cesta punta individual y perdió la de mano parejas.

articles.title: Bristol overcome Exeter to go third in Prem
articles.summary: Bristol move up to third place in the Prem after beating Exeter 20-7 at Ashton Gate.
articles.body:
Tries: Ibitoye, Ivanishvili Cons: Williams 2 Pens: Williams 2

Bristol moved up to third place in the Prem after beating Exeter 20-7 at Ashton Gate.

Gabriel Ibitoye's 26th-minute try and James Williams' penalty three minutes later were the only scores of an attritional first half in difficult conditions.

Greg Fisilau was mauled over 12 minutes after the restart as Exeter got on the scoreboard.

The Chiefs tried to force a second, but it was Bristol that earned the win when Williams kicked an excellent 41-metre penalty before Luca Ivanishvili crashed over from close range after Olly Woodburn had fumbled a high ball.

His late try denied Exeter a losing bonus point and leaves Rob Baxter's side in ninth place on eight points, six behind the Bears.

The stormy weather's impact was in evidence from the first whistle as both sides struggled to keep hold of the ball.

Bristol almost scored in the opening 60 seconds after an Exeter mistake under a kick saw the ball bobble around in their in-goal area.

It was as close as either side came to scoring in the opening 26 minutes as the hosts had the better of the possession and territory but were stifled by a spirited Exeter defence.

The pressure finally told when Ibitoye got on the end of a looping Harry Randall pass and beat Zack Wimbush to dive into the left corner.

Williams' penalty soon after extended the lead to 10 points and Exeter then had Australia star Tom Hooper forced off with a shoulder injury just before the interval.

Despite that setback, Henry Slade almost dotted down a Sam Wolstenholme grubber kick four minutes after the restart before Exeter's maul got them back into the game soon after.

First the pack earned themselves a penalty and the second maul from the resulting lineout 10 metres out saw Fisilau forced over.

The Chiefs forwards won another penalty inside the 22 with eight minutes left, but superb work from Ibitoye saw the Bears turn the ball over six metres out.

Bristol went straight up the field and a penalty resulting from a high tackle was dispatched well by Williams despite the tough conditions.

And the weather proved to be a distraction for Woodburn soon after as he missed a high kick and was put under pressure by Ibitoye, who was stopped inches from the Exeter line.

But eight phases later Georgian replacement Ivanishvili forced his way over to seal a hard-fought victory.

articles.title: Köln's René Wagner responds to critique after draw with Schalke
articles.summary: Köln managed to keep their first clean sheet this season and also was René Wagner's first clean sheet for Köln in the 0-0 draw with Schalke at home on Sunday...
articles.body:
Köln managed to keep their first clean sheet this season and also was René Wagner's first clean sheet for Köln in the 0-0 draw with Schalke at home on Sunday.

However, the home side controlled possession for the majority of the game and left a fair few chances behind whilst not putting enough pressure on Schalke during periods of the tie.

With strikers Ragnar Ache, Thijs Dallinga and Imad Rondić all out with injuries the Billy Goats went through a second game in a row without scoring despite chances including most notably a big chance for substitute Luca Waldschmidt.

After the match, the fans in the stadium's infamous Südkurve started whistling and around the ground some unhappy fans started to chant for the manager's exit.

Manager René Wagner sympathised partly with this after the tie as he said: "It feels a bit too little to come away from this game with this result."

Wagner was also asked about the reaction from the fans in the stadium after the game but he defended the performance and also the decision to take off winger Mikey Moore.

In defending his team and the performance, he said: "It's part of the job to try and win a game like this at home. We felt like we did this but the precision in the final third was not enough."

articles.title: Spurs seal rare win at Chelsea as Palmer sees red
articles.summary: Tottenham clinched a Premier League win at Chelsea for just the second time in 36 years as a woeful own goal from Blues keeper Mike Penders was followed by C...
articles.body:
Tottenham clinched a Premier League win at Chelsea for just the second time in 36 years as a woeful own goal from Blues keeper Mike Penders was followed by Cole Palmer's red card in Saturday's 2-0 victory.

Roberto De Zerbi's side clinched their second successive league win thanks to Penders's howler in the second half at a rain-lashed Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea forward Palmer was sent off for a second booking moments later before Mathys Tel produced a superb solo effort to condemn the Blues to their first home defeat against Tottenham since 2018.

Since 1990, Tottenham had won just once in 41 previous away matches against London rivals Chelsea in all competitions.

Ending that miserable run gave Tottenham only their second win in their last 16 league games against Chelsea, both home and away, and their first since 2023.

After a dismal start to the season, Tottenham have climbed to 12th place after building on Monday's win against Coventry, which ended their wait for a first league win this season.

It was a bitter blow for fourth-placed Chelsea, who had beaten Bournemouth and Everton in their previous two league games.

They were booed off at full-time and remain very much a work in progress under Xabi Alonso in the Spaniard's first season in charge.

With Joao Pedro sidelined by a late injury, Morgan Rogers was Chelsea's central striker, but their revamped attack was short of bite.

Teed up by Rogers after Pedro Neto stole possession from Mateus Fernandes, Palmer went close to an early opener with a curler that Antonin Kinsky tipped over at full stretch.

Tottenham responded with a spell of probing pressure as Omar Marmoush met Andy Robertson's cross with a shot that was repelled by Penders.

Alonso's men pieced together the best move of the half with a flurry of one-touch passes to reach Jordan Henderson on the edge of the area, but the midfielder's low drive was palmed away by Kinsky.

Neto tested Kinsky with a fierce blast but the Tottenham keeper was up to the task with a save at his near post.

Tottenham suffered a blow when often-injured midfielder James Maddison limped off in a premature end to only his second start since May 2025.

Maddison had already missed training sessions since his long-awaited start against Coventry and his latest fitness setback suggested it was a failed gamble to start him at the Bridge.

In keeping with the sloppy fare, Neto fired straight at Kinsky from a dangerous position after Palmer pounced on Sandro Tonali's wayward pass.

When Palmer's run was halted by Fernandes's handball, the Chelsea star escaped with a yellow card after barging into his rival with such aggression that the Tottenham midfielder was sent crashing to the sodden turf.

Tottenham exacted swift revenge in the 77th minute.

Fernandes's in-swinging corner should have been caught by Penders, but he opted for a punch that was completely mistimed as he diverted the ball into his net for a comical own goal.

It was a horrible moment for the 21-year-old Penders, who was making his first league start in the absence of Emiliano Martinez following jaw surgery.

Rubbing salt into Chelsea's wounds, Palmer was dismissed three minutes later for an ugly stamp on Conor Gallagher.

Tel wrapped up Tottenham's memorable triumph in fitting style in the 87th minute, skipping away from Chelsea's flat-footed defence to drill a fine finish into the bottom corner from the edge of the area.

articles.title: NASCAR qualifying at Talladega sets Sunday lineup for Chase race
articles.summary: Three races remain in the 2026 NASCAR season before champions are crowned in the Cup, O'Reilly and Truck Series. Sunday's race is at Talladega.
articles.body:
Chase Briscoe and Austin Hill were fastest in Saturday qualifying and have earned the front row for Sunday's YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway. Briscoe averaged 186.065 around the 2.66-mile tri-oval; he was the only driver to surpass 186.

Given the nature of big-pack racing at Talladega, Sunday's race has been pointed to as a potential season-wrecker (quite literally) for those within range of winning the Cup Series championship.

articles.title: Johnstone To Keep His Place? | Predicted 4-2-3-1 Celtic Lineup To Face Hibernian
articles.summary: Despite breaking the deadlock early in the second half, Celtic conceded twice within minutes to Celta Vigo and suffered another European defeat on Thursday n...
articles.body:
Despite breaking the deadlock early in the second half, Celtic conceded twice within minutes to Celta Vigo and suffered another European defeat on Thursday night. They now travel to Easter Road to face Hibernian, and the Hoops must take all three points to maintain their cushion at the top of the Premiership.

Hibs, stuck at rock bottom in the table, are having a nightmare with just two wins in 9 games. David Gray's dismissal has not changed their fortune, with new boss Marink Reedijk losing to Dundee United and Falkirk since succeeding the Scotsman. Celtic clinched identical 2-1 wins in Edinburgh when they visited Hibernian last season, and the home side need to punch above their weight to script an upset on Sunday afternoon.

Predicted 4-2-3-1 Celtic Lineup To Face Hibernian

Martin O'Neill restored Sam Johnstone in goal against Celta Vigo, replacing Viljami Sinisalo. The veteran custodian might now keep his place, having lost it to the Finnish shotstopper following their shambolic 3-0 defeat to Old Firm rivals Rangers before the international break.

GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – MAY 10: James Forrest of Celtic shoots at goal during the William Hill Premiership match between Celtic FC and Hibernian FC at Celtic Park on May 10, 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Alistair Johnston is back in team training but must not be rushed into action, given his recurring injury problems. Colby Donovan should get the nod on the right ahead of Anthony Ralston and Jordan Lotomba, but the gaffer could drop Liam Scales and restore Auston Trusty to partner with Dane Murray in deep defence. Kieran Tierney is expected to retain his left-back spot over Landon Emenalo.

Skipper Callum McGregor, a shadow of his earlier self, is likely to feature again as a deep-lying playmaker. The Bhoys lack a like-for-like replacement for the Scottish midfielder, but could rely on versatile Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain to manage his minutes in the middle of the park. Mika Baur must showcase his box-to-box movements and down-the-middle runs while pairing up with McGregor as the 'double pivot'.

Benjamin Nygren has been scrutinised for his lack of work ethic as a 'number 10'. But the Swedish ace has been consistent with his goals and assists, cementing his spot over Oliver Sorensen and Luke McCowan. Haissem Hassan and Callum Osmand must operate from the flanks; however, the latter's minutes should be managed carefully as he could not complete the Hearts and Celta fixtures due to fitness reasons. Hyun-jun Yang remains sidelined, but James Forrest, Sebastian Tounekti and Jota could feature from the bench as second-half substitutes.

Kasper Hogh should fight for his place, as he lost the starting status to Camilo Duran, who is in flying form while spearheading the attack.

articles.title: Packers fan survey says Christian Watson will finish 2026 as top receiver
articles.summary: Watson has a slight lead in this week’s survey.
articles.body:
Matthew Golden, drops aside, is on a hot streak. He has hit the century mark in receiving yardage in two straight games and has nearly closed the gap on Christian Watson for the team lead in receiving yards. Watson still has a slight edge, but both players are over 500 yards on the season, making them the only receiver tandem in the NFL to have reached that mark after Week 6.

We asked Packers fans this week which player was the one they thought would finish the season as the team's leader in receiving yardage. While Golden got a substantial share of the vote, Watson still came out on top with 61% of the responses favoring him over Golden. The second-year pro received a solid 36 percent vote share, however, with "other" coming in at just three percent.

It seems that sportsbooks are extremely evenly split on who they expect to be the Packers' WR1 to be moving forward. For the Packers' Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions, FanDuel Sportsbook has the over/unders on receiving yards set extremely closely: Christian Watson's number is 74.5, while Golden is one yard short of that number at 73.5.

As for overall fan confidence, the win over the Cowboys has Packers fans continuing to tick upward in their general sentiments. After last week's confidence index grew back over 50 percent for the first time since early in the season, that number is now up to 76% with the Lions on deck.

Keep it here at APC for full coverage of Sunday's game in Detroit to see if the Packers can keep their winning streak going.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton tops the timing sheets in FP3 ahead of Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc
articles.summary: A fight for pole position between Red Bull and Ferrari could be in the cards at the United States Grand Prix
articles.body:
AUSTIN, Texas — Lewis Hamilton topped the timing sheets in the third and final hour of practice ahead of Max Verstappen and teammate Charles Leclerc, setting up what could be a dramatic qualifying hour here at the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix.

The session got underway right at 12:30 p.m. local time, under partly cloudy skies with the air temperature right at 80 degrees Fahrenheit. And a few teams did not waste any time, with Sergio Pérez, Gabriel Bortoleto, and Franco Colapinto taking to the track right as the green light appeared at the end of pit lane.

A few other teams, however, took a more relaxed approach at the start, as drivers such as Lando Norris, Verstappen, Oscar Piastri, Leclerc, and Oliver Bearman remained in the garage, waiting to take to the track. And when Bortoleto dipped back down pit lane, Pérez and Colapinto had the track to themselves.

Gasly soon joined the fray, as did Valtteri Bottas, and as the clock struck 53 minutes remaining the Cadillac and Alpine duos had the track all to themselves.

Things started to pick up at the 50-minute mark, as more cars took to the track. Soon some more representative times would be coming in, as at the 47-minute mark Gasly topped the timing sheets with a 1:37.592, a time set on the C3 medium tire.

Hamilton then took that spot with a 1:36.716, posted on a set of softs, as the times started to come in, and tumble.

The first big surprises came with around 43 minutes left in FP3, as Liam Lawson jumped to the top of the timing sheets with a 1:36.420, set on a set of C3 medium tires. His spot at the top would not last long as Piastri nipped him with a 1:36.243 on the softs, and then Max Verstappen pumped in a 1:35.702 on the mediums.

Hamilton then responded, delivering a lap of 1:35.561 to rocket to the top of the board.

At the midpoint of FP2 the top five on the board were Hamilton, Verstappen, Norris, George Russell, and Isack Hadjar. While the teams and names might not be a surprise, the tire choices might have been. While Hamilton, Norris, and Russell set those times on the C4 soft tires, Hadjar and Verstappen had set those on the C3 mediums.

That spoke to the pace with the RB22 for both Saturday … and Sunday.

Two more names entered the mix as the second half of FP3 opened. Leclerc went to the top on a set of medium tires – perhaps speaking to both Ferrari's pace and the small upgrades the team brought to Austin – and then Drivers' Championship leader Kimi Antonelli slid into third, on a set of the soft tires.

Things did get a little sporty at one moment, with Russell, Esteban Ocon, and Nico Hülkenberg treating the proceedings like Sunday rather than Saturday:

At the 20-minute mark, many of the top drivers were in the garage, including the Ferrari pair as well as Verstappen and the McLaren duo. But Antonelli was in full attack mode, using a fresh set of C4 soft tires that had been bolted onto his W17. Behind him? His Mercedes teammate Russell, also with a fresh set of soft tires.

Antonelli went purple through the first sector and purple through the second as he tracked 0.414 second ahead of the benchmark time set by Leclerc. He came home with a lap time of 1:35.015, a new benchmark and a clear warning to the rest of the grid.

But it was for naught, as his time was deleted for exceeding track limits at Turn 9.

Then it was Verstappen's turn, as Red Bull bolted a set of soft tires onto his RB22. He went fastest through the first sector, and was still up on Leclerc through the second sector. Verstappen came home with a time of 1:35.061, setting a new standard for the session.

That standard lasted only a few seconds, as Hamilton cut the beam with a 1:34.893.

Finally we got a representative lap on the softs from Leclerc, and it put Ferrari's other driver to the top, as he delivered a 1:34.810, just ahead of Hamilton in P2.

However, that lap was soon deleted as well, with Leclerc having exceeded track limits at Turn 10.

Track limits might be something to watch during qualifying later today, after an astonishing 207 lap times were deleted over the two practice sessions on Friday, and race officials relaxed track limits at several spots on the track, including Turns 12, 15 and 20.

With under ten minutes remaining, perhaps the biggest surprise was the driver sitting in P7 as it was none other than Hülkenberg sitting well inside the top ten. Could he and Audi be setting up a Q3 shock for later in the day?

Hülkenberg might, but his teammate could be in a bit of hot water, as race officials noted Gabriel Bortoleto for potentially impeding Hamilton during a push lap in the final minutes of the session.

And in those final minutes of the session, there was a bit of drama from the Red Bull pair. First it was from Verstappen as he locked up his RB22 entering Turn 15, and sent smoke flying on the track as he flat-spotted the tires. Then it was Hadjar locking up at Turn 1, as he came upon Alexander Albon on the racing line. The two drivers had a bit of a … moment on the track before driving off their separate ways.

When the checkered flag flew, it was still Hamilton at the top of the board, followed by Verstappen, Leclerc, Antonelli, and Russell rounding out the top five. Piastri slotted in sixth, followed by Hülkenberg, Norris, Gasly, and Hadjar to close out the top ten spots.

Liam Lawson clocked in at P11, followed by teammate Arvid Lindblad in P12. Bortoleto, Bearman, Colapinto, Alonso, Ocon, Stroll, Albon, Sainz, Pérez, and Bottas rounded out the rest of the grid.

What does this all mean for qualifying later today?

It might mean we'll have a shootout on our hands here in Austin.

articles.title: Giants Prepare for Return of $54 Million Free Agent Bust
articles.summary: New York Giants prepare for return of $54 million free-agent bust. The post Giants Prepare for Return of $54 Million Free Agent Bust appeared first on HEAVY.
articles.body:
It's time for New York Giants cornerback Paulson Adebo to resurrect his NFL career — something that's been in shambles since he lost his starting spot to Deonte Banks in training camp then landed on injured reserve after a Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys.

After missing the last five games, Adebo is set to return from injured reserve in Week 7, as the Giants head into a critical road game against the Houston Texans.

"Paulson Adebo will be activated from IR later today," ESPN's Jordan Raanan wrote on his official X account on Saturday morning. "'He's ready to go,' John Harbaugh said on Friday. With Greg Newsome (concussion) out, Adebo could be right back in starting mix."

"Paulson Adebo will be activated from IR later today," Fireside Giants wrote on X. "Some much needed depth at cornerback set to return from injury."

Adebo is in the second season of a whopping 3-year, $54 million free-agent contract he signed with the Giants before the 2025 season.

Adebo Roasted for Losing Starting Role to Banks

Losing his starting spot to Banks, who had been written off as an all-time 1st-round bust, led to some pretty virulent online blowback against Adebo — as to be expected when you're getting paid $18 million per year.

"The Giants unofficial Week 1 depth chart lists Donte Banks alongside Greg Newsome as the starting cornerbacks," Raanan wrote on his official X account on September 8. "Banks ahead of Paulson Adebo Chauncey Golston is listed as the starting DE alongside DT Shelby Harris and NT D.J. Reader . Golston ahead of Darius Alexander ."

"If the depth chart is legit, my god … Paulson Adebo, how did you lose a starting job to Deonte Banks!!!" Empire State Media's Alex Wilson wrote on his official X account. "I'm excited to see if Banks turns things around, but man, what a colossal waste of money on Adebo if true."

"The Giants paid Paulson Adebo good money to be CB1," Gridiron Media wrote on its official X account. "After one year, he's a backup. Joe Schoen is just awful."

Deonte Banks Began Making Moves in Training Camp

Banks began breathing life into what seemed like a DOA career at the start of training camp — the 1st under new head coach John Harbaugh and defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson.

After being benched and relegated to a return specialist role in 2025, the No. 23 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft seemed destined for another season as a backup in 2026.

"There is serious competition for the Giants starting cornerback positions," Big Blue Film Room wrote on its official X account on August 8. "Deonte Banks (is) in that mix. Banks ranked 112th out of 114 qualifying cornerbacks last season in PFF grade. But he's earned rave reviews in camp in Dennard Wilson's new system."

articles.body:
After a long negotiating period, DirecTV announced a new multiyear distribution agreement with the NHL on Saturday to distribute numerous streaming services, including Minnesota's new Wild+.

The Wild's new TV deal has not been a smooth transition, resulting in numerous sports bars across the state not being able to show the games. Even more fans haven't been able to watch the games at home. DirecTV is one of the biggest cable providers in the state, and its users can now watch the Wild in Minnesota.

"We are committed to keeping fans connected to their favorite teams and giving them more choice and flexibility in how they watch and what they pay," Rob Thun, chief content officer at DirecTV, said in a release. "As local sports distribution evolves, DIRECTV brings team channels, regional sports networks, and other viewing options together to make it easier for fans to follow the teams they love. We're pleased to work with the NHL, NBA, MLB, and others to deliver that experience."

The next opportunity to watch the Wild is Saturday night, when they play the Seattle Kraken at 9 p.m. CT. They play again Sunday against the Vancouver Canucks at 9 p.m.

A resounding 4-0 win over SC Elversberg earlier today was more than enough reason for Martin Demichelis to smile after their day's work.

"After two defeats, we had to get back to winning ways today. We were up against a tricky opponent and the first half wasn't easy.

"The changes we made helped us match their intensity, and our quality made the difference in front of goal," Demichelis said after the game.

"A lot of people probably thought I was taking too much of a risk [with 8 changes]. But five of the players in today's line-up also played in Munich a week ago.

"I see how hard they work in training. Keeping a clean sheet was important too," the Argentine explained with a smile.

Making his return from a long-term injury layoff, Christoph Baumgartner was another happy face soaking up the win in the mixed zone.

"First of all, huge credit to Elversberg. They're doing an incredible job and they caused us quite a few problems.

"We made a few adjustments at half time and did a better job of finding space in front of their defence and making runs in behind.

We've also got the individual quality to make the difference. Getting that first goal was crucial."

"After such a memorable moment for me personally at the Bernabéu, I was really looking forward to playing at home again.

"The most important thing is that we won, but to come back after so long and score straight away is pretty cool," the Austria concluded.

Leipzig's attention will now turn to preparations for their DFB-Pokal second round fixture away to Rot Weiss Essen next Tuesday.

articles.title: Scott Boras Lays Out Tarik Skubal Free Agency Outlook Ahead of Dodgers Talks
articles.summary: Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal is entering free agency, and his renowned agent, Scott Boras, discussed his client's status.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal is entering free agency, and his renowned baseball agent, Scott Boras, discussed his marquee client's free-agent status.

Boras is known for being an aggressive negotiator who typically refuses contract extensions throughout a player's career, letting them enter free agency and letting the free market decide their ultimate value.

When it comes to getting the best possible deal for his clients, especially the top ones, no one in baseball has a more stellar reputation.

However, while that often benefits his clients, teams can struggle to lock down their players when Boras is in the mix.

With Skubal, Boras is in a position to do what he does best: explore the market, try to spark a bidding war, and land a massive deal that should break records.

Skubal's status as one of the best pitchers alive makes a sales pitch unnecessary. Boras, when speaking to The Athletic's Andy McCullough , made an interesting statement that relays how he views his client.

"Last time around, everybody talked about Skuby Doo. It's kind of like, with Skubal now, it's Skuby Done. He's proven it at all levels, in different markets, in different environments," Boras told The Athletic.

How long will it take for Skubal to sign?

Boras is typically not shy about waiting for the best possible deal and letting some teams panic about getting a deal done.

With a lockout coming on December 1st, Boras thinks teams will be highly motivated to secure players before a new set of rules comes into place.

"For many teams, I can make an argument it's clearly best for them to sign players currently, before the (new) CBA, than it is after," Boras told The Athletic.

"Because they have more freedom to do what they're going to do. They can react later. Now they can get the talent. They can get what they want."

The Dodgers, who will be talking to Boras , and the rest of the league, will need to make their pitches and offers quickly and be ready to negotiate fast, because the best player in free agency may not be available for long.

articles.title: Juventus Women-Roma | Match Report
articles.summary: Juventus Women suffered a 5-2 defeat to Roma on Matchday 4 of Serie A Women. At the Pozzo-La Marmora Stadium in Biella, the visitors took control of the matc...
articles.body:
Juventus Women suffered a 5-2 defeat to Roma on Matchday 4 of Serie A Women. At the Pozzo-La Marmora Stadium in Biella, the visitors took control of the match in the first half. The Bianconere responded after the break, pulling two goals back through Redondo and Pavan, but were unable to complete the comeback.

Roma started brightly and broke the deadlock after just four minutes, with Giugliano finding the net from distance. The visitors doubled their lead in the 10th minute through Pellegrino Cimò, who was set up by Rieke, before Corelli made it 3-0 three minutes later, getting ahead of Carbonell to score from a free-kick delivery.

Juventus looked to respond and came close in the 18th minute when Salvai's header was saved by Baldi. Five minutes later, Sarriegi tried to find space inside the Roma penalty area but was denied by a defensive intervention from Oladipo.

The Bianconere threatened again towards the end of the half, with Chiba testing Baldi with a left-footed effort in the 45th minute. However, deep into stoppage time, Roma were awarded a penalty for a Pinto handball, with the decision confirmed following an FVS review. Giugliano made no mistake from the spot to send the visitors into the break with a 4-0 lead.

THE BIANCONERE FIGHT BACK AFTER THE BREAK

Juventus made two changes at half-time, with Noordman and Pavan replacing Chiba and Sarriegi, as the Bianconere looked to change the momentum of the match.

Roma thought they had added a fifth goal four minutes into the second half through Pellegrino Cimò, but the effort was ruled out for offside. Five minutes later, Juventus pulled a goal back: Noordman delivered a low cross into the box and Redondo was on hand to turn the ball home and make it 4-1.

The Bianconere continued to push forward and came close to scoring again in the 69th minute through Librán, who had replaced Bartel shortly before. The midfielder controlled the ball inside the area before firing narrowly over the crossbar.

Juventus found their second goal in the 77th minute, with Redondo turning provider for Pavan, who finished to reduce the deficit to two goals.

Isaac Guerrero's side kept pressing and almost added a third in the 87th minute, when Redondo's header flew just over the bar. However, a minute later, Bergamaschi found the net to make it 5-2 and seal the victory for Roma.

Juventus were ultimately left empty-handed after a match shaped by Roma's strong first-half display and the Bianconere's response after the break.

articles.summary: Liverpool might be making even more moves on the attacking front very soon. If anything the Reds frontline looks the most complete part of Andoni Iraola's ji...
articles.body:
Liverpool might be making even more moves on the attacking front very soon.

If anything the Reds frontline looks the most complete part of Andoni Iraola's jigsaw. However, last summer Liverpool spent the last few days of the window pursuing another attacker.

Ismailar Sarr and Yankuba Minteh were potential targets. However, ultimately Liverpool were priced out of those moves.

But in hindsight looking at Liverpool's attacking options right now, they look pretty solid.

Bradley Barcola looks to be a strong addition. Alexander Isak is firing on all cylinders. Florian Wirtz is now getting goal contributions. Victor Munoz might have been a steal. Rio Ngumoha could be one of the best wingers on the planet soon. And then there's Lewis Koumas, who has become a fan favourite for his voracious work ethic.

And then there's Hugo Ekitike of course. He's slowly getting ready to make a comeback and there are high hopes he can return to the same form that he played in before.

Behind them, Will Wright is banging in goals for the U21s and U19s and will likely be getting a chance in the first-team soon. Liverpool's new recruit Djylian N'Guessan could also be joining the Reds in the January window, and he is also very highly rated.

Joshua Abe on the wings is regarded as one of the best young prospects at the club. AJ Yeguo is making a strong case for that as well.

And Erik Farkas and Samuel Martinez are two players who Liverpool believe can rival Wirtz's no.10 role in the first-team very soon.

Julian Ward ready to sign Mathis Albert for Liverpool

The club's new sporting director has made it clear he wants to sign young players. Ward's entire philosophy hinges on building for the future.

And while there are a lot of exciting attackers, it has never stopped him before from adding more.

Bild as per Get Football News Germany are reporting that Liverpool are among the club's interested in 17-year-old Mathis Albert from Borussia Dortmund.

This is a generational winger, who is already on the fringes of the first-team of the Bundesliga giants and who has dazzled with his one vs one ability in a myriad of youth tournaments.

Albert could be the final missing piece of the jigsaw in attack for Iraola. Liverpool are clearly ready to sign another attacker and this signing has Ward's fingerprints written all over it.

articles.summary: The UConn commit broke the Connecticut record with his 51st career TD catch in the second quarter.
articles.body:
WATERBURY - Holy Cross High senior wide receiver Dae'Sean Graves came into Saturday morning's game at Crosby one touchdown catch away from tying the state's all-time career record, and two away from breaking it.

It took a little bit of time, but the UConn commit caught touchdowns of 37 and 6 yards from senior quarterback Brady Lombardo to become the state record holder with 51 career touchdown receptions. Holy Cross beat Crosby 52-13 and improved to 5-1.

Graves broke Southington star Alex Jamele's former record of 50, set in 2014, by catching two touchdowns in the final minutes of the first half.

After a fumble recovery by the Crusader defense, Graves went deep and Lombardo hit him for a 37-yard touchdown pass with 2:24 left in the second quarter to tie Jamele's record. Holy Cross got the ball back with 50.1 seconds left in the first half, and Graves caught a 33-yard pass from Lombardo to get the ball to the Crosby 6-yard line.

After an incomplete pass, Graves came in motion, moving from right to left. Lombardo caught the snap and pitched it forward to Graves on a jet pass. Graves broke a tackle at the goal line to score and break Jamele's record.

The entire Crusader offensive unit joined Graves in the end zone to celebrate.

Graves finished with eight catches for 132 yards and the two touchdowns, and all of it came in the first half. He is 10 catches away from tying East Catholic star Joey Montalvo's state record of 226, which was set last year. Graves now has 3,229 career receiving yards, which puts him 642 yards away from tying Montalvo's record of 3,871, which was also set last year.

As if Graves didn't have a big enough morning, he also returned an interception 39 yards for a touchdown. Freshman Anthony Serrano also had an interception return for a score for Holy Cross.

Besides the two touchdowns to Graves, Lombardo threw scoring passes of 68 yards to Aaden Hall and 10 yards to Tyler Smith.

Raquim Chapman scored the first touchdown of the game on a 1-yard sneak for Crosby (2-4). Kayden Myers ran for a 17-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter.
