articles.title: Auburn football's Jacob Strand exits game vs LSU with injury
articles.summary: Auburn football offensive lineman Jacob Strand exited Auburn football's game against LSU. What we know.
articles.body:
AUBURN — It's been a tough day for Auburn football. Already trailing to LSU by three scores, Auburn saw its fourth player hit the turf with an injury on Saturday, Oct. 24.

This time it was starting offensive tackle Jacob Strand. The offensive line had already allowed two sacks and has had issues getting the run game going against LSU.

Backup offensive lineman Jo Simmons filled in for Strand, who went down down tapping his helmet. Strand got up and walked off the field on his own power.

Strand is the second offensive lineman to be injured against LSU. Kenneth McManus IV went down earlier in the game but returned the next offensive drive.

Jaeden Day covers high school sports, Alabama State football and Auburn recruiting for the Montgomery Advertiser/USA Today. You can find him on X at dayjaeden12 , or reach him at JDay@montgome.gannett.com .

articles.title: Syracuse gets major boost back for Saturday night at UNC
articles.summary: Steve Angeli played high-level football to start 2025, before tearing his achilles. After another injury this fall, Angeli returns Saturday night.
articles.body:
With fourth quarter comebacks in each of their past two football games, the North Carolina Tar Heels are fun to watch. UNC (4-2, 2-1 ACC) upset 25th-ranked Pitt on October 10, then stole back the Victory Bell at archival Duke .

North Carolina makes its long-awaited return home on Saturday night, hosting Syracuse at 7:30 p.m. in a battle of ACC teams headed in opposite directions. The Orange (2-4, 0-2 ACC) are better than their record shows, losing three one-score games, while the Tar Heels are looking for their first 3-game winning streak since 2024.

Syracuse will be getting a much-needed boost back for its offense. On Friday, On3 Sports' Pete Nakos reported Orange quarterback Steve Angeli is expected to start against UNC.

Angeli started each of Syracuse's first three games, before losing his starting spot and injuring his leg. With Malachi Nelson and Amari Odom out, Angeli gets his chance to shine.

Angeli was one of college football's top surprises in 2025, leading Syracuse to a 3-1 start and road upset of Clemson . In Death Valley, though, Angeli tore his achilles and the Orange lost their final eight games.

Take away the second half at Clemson this year and losing to Notre Dame, the Tar Heels are good at defending the pass. With Duke (5-2, 2-2 ACC) driving in the closing seconds of last week's Victory Bell battle, freshman Kenton Dopson III picked off Walker Eget's pass to seal the North Carolina win.

Greg Smith and Kaleb Cost are leaders in the secondary. Linebackers Derek McDonald and Peyton Seelmann always have their eyes on the quarterback. Xavier Lewis and Leroy Jackson headline a deep, defensive line that excels at getting into the backfield.

Syracuse will thrive in Angeli's return, but how much? UNC will look to its defense for a third-straight victory on Saturday night, hopefully in front of a packed Kenan Stadium crowd.

articles.title: DAZN has bigger ambitions in U.S. sports as LA Kings partnership opens door to regional expansion
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — For years, DAZN has been best known to American sports fans as a destination for boxing and combat sports.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — For years, DAZN has been best known to American sports fans as a destination for boxing and combat sports. Around the world, however, the streaming platform has established itself as one of the largest sports broadcasters, carrying everything from European soccer and Formula One to the NFL and NHL.

Now, with the Los Angeles Kings among a growing collection of professional sports teams calling DAZN their local streaming home, the company is making an aggressive push into the United States with ambitions that extend far beyond regional sports television.

Walker Jacobs, DAZN's global chief revenue officer and president of DAZN USA, told The Sporting Tribune in an exclusive interview that the company's recent expansion into regional sports is only the first step in a much larger strategy to establish itself as a leading sports broadcaster in the United States.

"Our strategy was never and is not still to be a regional sports broadcaster," Jacobs said. "That's not what our strategy is. Our strategy is to be a leading sports broadcaster, full stop."

In the past six months, the London-based company has acquired local streaming rights involving 19 professional teams across Major League Baseball, the NBA, NHL and WNBA. The collection includes franchises such as the Kings, Memphis Grizzlies, Indiana Pacers, San Antonio Spurs, New York Knicks and New York Yankees.

For DAZN, the opportunity emerged as the traditional regional sports television model continued to experience financial difficulties, leaving teams searching for new distribution partners and fans wondering where they would be able to watch their favorite teams.

"Regional sports presented itself as a really attractive opportunity for us to get a foothold in several key U.S. markets," Jacobs said. "The rights became available. There was another major company that was involved that hit some financial trouble. There was a season that was about to start and teams had to make quick decisions."

That combination of circumstances allowed DAZN to enter markets that might otherwise have taken years to penetrate.

"What we hope this does is get millions of people using our product that have not used our product before," Jacobs said. "We believe that we have the best sports streaming product in the world. And we believe that once somebody comes on and starts using our product and tries our product, it's really hard to go back."

The Kings represent an important piece of that strategy in Southern California.

Beginning with the 2026-27 NHL season, DAZN became the exclusive direct-to-consumer streaming home for available locally televised Kings games through a partnership with Angels Broadcast Television (ABTV). Fans within the team's local television territory can watch games through DAZN with a direct subscription or, where eligible, authenticate using an existing television provider.

The service also includes pregame and postgame coverage, original programming and additional Kings-related content designed to give fans a more comprehensive experience than simply watching games.

Jacobs said the Kings partnership illustrates how DAZN hopes to differentiate itself from traditional regional sports networks while taking advantage of the company's enormous international reach.

DAZN distributes NHL.TV in most countries outside the United States and Canada, giving international subscribers access to NHL games through a single streaming product. While its Kings partnership is focused on Southern California, its relationship with the NHL creates a separate connection to hockey fans around the world.

"We have a local relationship with the team through our relationship with ABTV," Jacobs said. "On top of that, we have a relationship with the NHL for NHL.TV that's in most countries in the world."

"While we don't have a national broadcast partnership in the U.S. or Canada right now with the NHL, we're kind of bookending that with the local package we have with ABTV and then with the international package we have with NHL.TV."

The international reach is something few regional sports broadcasters can match.

DAZN carries major European soccer properties, including Serie A in Italy, Bundesliga in Germany and La Liga in Spain, along with Formula One in Spain. The company also has international NFL distribution rights and operates FIFA's streaming platform globally.

Jacobs, who oversees both DAZN's U.S. operations and its global revenue business, said the company has become one of the largest sports media companies in approximately 10 or 11 countries.

That global infrastructure provides an advantage as American professional sports leagues increasingly look beyond their domestic markets to grow their audiences.

But Jacobs emphasized that DAZN's immediate priority is much simpler: Make sure fans can find their games and watch them without problems.

That has become an increasingly complicated proposition for American sports fans as games migrate from traditional cable television to a growing number of streaming services.

In Los Angeles alone, fans have watched teams move across different platforms and distribution arrangements, sometimes without knowing where games would be available until shortly before a season begins.

Jacobs acknowledged the confusion surrounding the rapidly changing sports media landscape.

"I would agree with you. It feels a little all over the place sometimes," Jacobs said. "At the end of the day, the world's changing. How consumers are watching sports is changing and streaming is becoming a more and more important part of the mix."

DAZN has responded with an extensive marketing and communications strategy designed to educate fans about where they can watch games.

The company is working with teams to promote streaming availability through arena signage, email campaigns, digital advertising and other team-controlled platforms. It is also using paid media campaigns in each market to promote specific games and encourage subscriptions.

Jacobs believes some of the initial confusion will disappear once consumers become familiar with the platform.

"Change is always disruptive and change is always hard and it's always confusing," Jacobs said. "There'll always be people that say I wish it was the way it used to be. And that's a tale as old as time."

One of the ways DAZN hopes to convince fans to embrace that change is by offering more than live games.

The Kings' dedicated page on DAZN includes team programming and original content produced through ABTV, creating a destination for fans looking for more extensive coverage of the franchise.

For a team competing for attention in a crowded Los Angeles sports market, that additional programming could become an important part of the viewing experience.

"It's hugely important," Jacobs said. "That comes from our relationship with ABTV. I think they've really done a great job with their programming and their content strategy. In this particular case with the Kings, I think we're the beneficiary of that."

DAZN also plans to supplement its regional sports offerings with original programming of its own.

One upcoming project is a show featuring former NHL enforcer Ty Domi, scheduled to debut later this hockey season. The series will feature conversations with prominent athletes and entertainers, including Tom Brady, Mark Wahlberg, Alex Rodriguez, Shaquille O'Neal and Wayne Gretzky.

Jacobs believes programming like that can introduce hockey to a wider audience while giving existing fans additional reasons to spend time on the platform.

"What we're trying to do is figure out how all the parts come together to create something really interesting and really attractive to all types of fans," Jacobs said. "Having NHL legends sort of harken back to the glory days, and some of the great years that the Kings have had, we think is going to be a lot of fun."

The strategy also creates opportunities for DAZN to introduce fans of one sport to other sports they might not have previously followed.

Someone who subscribes to watch the Kings could eventually discover boxing, international soccer or original programming on the same platform. A basketball fan subscribing to watch the Spurs or Knicks could similarly become exposed to DAZN's broader sports portfolio.

That approach is central to the company's long-term growth plans.

DAZN has already strengthened its American boxing business through expanded relationships with Top Rank and Premier Boxing Champions while maintaining partnerships with Golden Boy Promotions and Matchroom.

Jacobs described those investments as a deliberate effort to make DAZN more relevant to American sports fans even before the company's regional sports expansion.

Now, with millions of potential new customers coming through its local team partnerships, DAZN hopes to use that increased audience to pursue additional programming and rights agreements.

"We want to attract more teams and more regional rights," Jacobs said. "If the leagues decide that they want to find a single solution to create a national solution for local rights, we want to be the obvious choice for them to go with."

That possibility could become increasingly significant as professional sports leagues evaluate whether to continue relying on individual local television agreements or pursue broader national distribution models for games that have traditionally been televised regionally.

Jacobs sees DAZN's current partnerships as an opportunity to demonstrate to leagues, teams and fans that the company can successfully handle those responsibilities.

"We hope that this year sort of gives us a trial run to demonstrate how great our product is and how much fans love it and how much our team partners respect working with us and vice versa," Jacobs said.

For now, however, Jacobs insists the company's most important responsibility is delivering a reliable experience for fans who simply want to watch their teams play.

"I think we have an order of operations of what the most important priorities are for us," Jacobs said. "The first and foremost is to deliver the live games with a great production quality, a great consumer experience, seamlessly and flawlessly."

Only after establishing that foundation does DAZN intend to focus on expanding engagement through on-demand programming, studio shows and additional sports rights.

"If we do that really well, I think we're going to have happy fans, happy consumers, happy customers, and happy partners," Jacobs said.

For Kings fans, the immediate impact is a new way to watch their team and access additional programming. For DAZN, the partnership represents something much larger: An entry point into one of the world's most valuable and competitive sports media markets.

And Jacobs made it clear that the company has no intention of stopping with the teams it has already signed.

"We've made it clear to all of our league partners around the world and all the major rights holders here in the U.S. that we want to be an important part of their consideration set moving forward," Jacobs said. "Our ambitions are much, much bigger than sort of being one-dimensional."

For a company that American sports fans once associated primarily with boxing, the Kings and DAZN's other regional sports partnerships could ultimately be remembered as the beginning of a much bigger transformation.

articles.title: Arsenal join Man City at Premier League summit, Spurs shock Chelsea 2-0
articles.summary: Gunners capitalise on City’s first loss of the season, while Spurs get second league win at Stamford Bridge in 36 years.
articles.body:
Arsenal joined Manchester City at the top of the Premier League table after a 2-0 ⁠victory over Everton in torrential rain at ⁠the Emirates Stadium on Saturday, capitalising on City’s first defeat of the season earlier in the day.

City had left the door open when they fell to a 2-1 loss at Aston Villa, where Nicolas Jackson struck twice to end the visitors’ perfect start to the league campaign.

Tottenham ⁠Hotspur stunned fourth-placed Chelsea 2-0 in only their second league victory at Stamford Bridge in 36 years, while Fulham beat Coventry City 1-0 for their second league victory of the season.

With the leaders beaten in Birmingham, Arsenal seized their chance to erase the three-point gap as goals from Ezri Konsa and Gabriel secured a comfortable win over Everton in ⁠soaking north London conditions.

The result moved Mikel Arteta’s side level on 21 points with City in what is already shaping up to be a closely fought title race after eight games, but one played under a cloud amid City’s off-field financial case .

Arsenal made their strong start count when Martin Odegaard’s corner caused chaos in the Everton box.

England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford kept out the initial danger after the ball was flicked on at the near post but, with Everton unable to clear, Konsa bundled home his first goal for the club from ‌a yard out in the seventh minute.

The set-piece goal was Arsenal’s first since May, ending a run of 13 games across all competitions without one.

“I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons; I know how tough it is to play against us,” Konsa said. “It’s not surprising to me.

“We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home, and we want to win as many games here as possible.”

Arsenal’s two milestone men combined to give the Gunners a two-goal cushion in the 68th minute, with Ben White marking his 200th appearance for the club by clipping a cross to the far post, where Gabriel headed home on his 200th Premier League appearance.

At Villa Park, Unai Emery’s team climbed to sixth on 11 points with their first home league victory ⁠this season and third successive league win over City, who are playing under the shadow of an independent commission’s findings that they ⁠committed 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules.

City have always denied any wrongdoing, and have appealed.

Jackson took advantage of two City blunders, opening the scoring in the sixth minute when defender Marc Guehi’s heavy touch allowed Villa captain John McGinn to pounce and feed the striker, who slotted the ball into the bottom corner.

Erling Haaland equalised soon after the break when he headed home Iliman Ndiaye’s clipped cross from a ⁠free kick.

But Jackson struck the winner on the hour when Ibrahim Mbaye surged down the right before cutting the ball back for his Senegal international teammate, whose shot sneaked under the diving body of keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

“It was incredible; we got the win, which is ⁠the most important thing. Man City are a strong team, the league leaders,” Jackson told TNT Sports. “It’s just ⁠the beginning; we’re trying to work game by game.”

Tottenham get rare win at Stamford Bridge

At Stamford Bridge, Spurs got on the scoresheet in the 77th minute when Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders punched a corner into his own net in his first league start.

Chelsea were reduced to 10 men when Cole Palmer was shown a second yellow card in the 80th minute for a late challenge on Conor Gallagher.

Mathys Tel sealed the victory for Spurs in the 87th when he gained ‌possession inside his own half before embarking on a surging run down the left, gliding past two defenders and firing a low shot from outside the box into the bottom corner.

“It’s very special, because we came here a lot of times and didn’t get a win,” said Tel. “And today, we made it together, all together, we showed great ‌mentality, ‌and I’m very happy about it.”

At Coventry, Fulham appeared ready to substitute Oscar Bobb before the winger produced a moment of quality in the 80th minute, driving into the box and curling a superb finish into the far corner.

Fulham are 13th in the table, while Coventry are 19th.

articles.title: WWE legend Ric Flair recovering after being hospitalized for fall
articles.summary: WWE legend Ric Flair was hospitalized after falling outside of a Florida restaurant while dealing with a blood clot in his leg. The 77-year-old retired American professional wrestler, whose real name is Richard Morgan Fliehr, said in an Instagram post Saturday that he spent the night in a Tampa hospital.
articles.body: WWE legend Ric Flair was hospitalized after falling outside of a Florida restaurant while dealing with a blood clot in his leg. The 77-year-old retired American professional wrestler, whose real name is Richard Morgan Fliehr, said in an Instagram post Saturday that he spent the night in a Tampa hospital. Flair had fallen outside a Wagamama restaurant in Tampa on Friday, cutting his head and eye, TMZ reported. “Thank You All For The Messages And Prayers! I Will Get Back To You Each Individually As I Get Stronger,” Flair wrote in a post Saturday. “Thank You To All The Tampa General Hospital Staff And Doctors That Put Up With Me Until 4:30am. I Appreciate You All And Thank You For Everything You Did For Me!” The wrestling icon said he’s on the mend. “I Am Focused On My Healing And Recovery Right Now,” he said, adding, “I Will Be Okay!” He shared a photo of himself smiling with a patch covering one of his eyes. His daughter, Charlotte Flair, a WWE wrestler, joked on X about that fall, saying: “Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head…(ps: he’s going to be ok).” Just hours before his fall, Flair had told his fans he had to cancel an appearance at the Washington State Horror Con in Seattle due to a blood clot in his leg. “Unfortunately, I Am Dealing With A Blood Clot In My Leg, And My Doctors Have Limited My Travel To 3–4 Hours. Seattle Falls Outside That Range, And As Disappointed As I Am, I Have To Put My Health And Recovery First,” he posted on Instagram Friday. Flair warned that blood clots are “extremely serious and can be life-threatening” and that he has a procedure scheduled to “strip the affected vein.” “I Look Forward To Getting Healthy And Seeing You All Down The Road. Thank You For The Love And Support,” he said Friday.

articles.title: Knicks try to clear up ‘misinformation’ about rings, say employees will get them in 4-6 weeks
articles.summary: The New York Knicks clear up “misinformation” Saturday, stating eligible staff will get championship rings within a month.
articles.body: The New York Knicks sought to clear up what they said is “misinformation” regarding the awarding of their championship rings, saying Saturday that employees who were always supposed to get them will do so in about a month. Madison Square Garden again conceded that using an email regarding the selection of rings to train staffers about cybersecurity was a mistake, though “reminding our employees to protect our IP was not.” It was the second straight day the NBA champions responded to criticism of their distribution of the jewelry they earned after winning their first title since 1973. Players were awarded their rings Tuesday night before the Knicks opened the season against the Philadelphia 76ers. But The Athletic reported later in the week that assistant coaches did not get theirs. Madison Square Garden responded to that Friday by saying more than 275 employees were already set to be gifted rings, worth more than $3.7 million. “There is a great deal of misinformation regarding the championship rings. The plan has always been to distribute more than 275 rings and jewelry to the people in the organization who were part of last season’s success,” an MSG spokesperson said Saturday. “As is common with many teams, the players were always supposed to get their rings as part of the opening night ceremony and then everyone else will receive theirs in about 4-6 weeks.” The Athletic report also said that in September, MSG employees received an email reading: “Congratulations, your Employee Championship Ring is here.” It showed a graphic with two ring styles that could be selected, but those who clicked on the link at the bottom of the email were forced to attend a mandatory cybersecurity class. “Regarding the phishing email, the process of securing and reminding our employees to protect our IP was not a mistake but the choice to use the ring to do so was a mistake and we apologize to our employees and the fans,” MSG said. “Winning the championship was a great moment for all New Yorkers. Those who choose to focus on the negative are missing the joy that comes with the team’s accomplishment.”

articles.title: Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream to even the WNBA Finals at 2-2
articles.summary: Gabby Williams scored 17 points and Golden State played stellar defense to beat the Atlanta Dream 67-62 on Saturday and even the WNBA Finals at 2-2.
articles.body: Gabby Williams scored 17 points and Golden State played stellar defense to beat the Atlanta Dream 67-62 on Saturday and even the WNBA Finals at 2-2. The best-of-seven series moves back to California on Monday for Game 5. The Valkyries stymied Atlanta star Angel Reese, holding her to just eight points. She had dominated the previous two games, averaging 25.5 points and 14 rebounds in the Dream victories. Reese struggled in Game 4, missing 10 of her 12 shots, including a few layups in the fourth quarter, after having double-doubles in each of the first three games. Tiffany Hayes was moved into the starting lineup Saturday and scored all of her 13 points in the second half as the Valkyries got their first victory since Game 1. “We just had to have more fight, more grit, and get back to us,” Hayes said in a TV interview after the game. “We still made a few mistakes but at the end of the day we played hard and we came out with the win.” Atlanta trimmed a 16-point halftime deficit to 61-55 midway through the fourth quarter, bringing fans in the sellout crowd of over 17,000 to their feet. Golden State answered with a 3-pointer by Veronica Burton to briefly silence them. The Dream then scored seven of the next nine points, including a three-point play by Rhyne Howard with 28 seconds left to get within 66-62. Burton then made the first of two free throws a second later and Atlanta couldn’t convert on the other end. Howard finished with 19 points for Atlanta, which shot just 33.3% overall and 4 for 23 from 3-point range. Golden State players had said between the 26-point Game 3 loss and Game 4 that they were confident they could win on Saturday and just needed to be more physical and play harder. They showed that grit on both ends of the court. Defensively, they challenged Atlanta shots led by Kiah Stokes and limited the Dream to few second-chance opportunities. Stokes finished with three blocks and now has a WNBA Finals record of 14 in the four games, surpassing the old record of 12 by Brittney Griner and Sylvia Fowles. Offensively, they limited turnovers, which had led to easy points for Atlanta in its two victories. The Valkyries also crashed the offensive boards, rebounding their own misses to give themselves more chances to score. Stokes had eight offensive rebounds of her 16 total. Coach Natalie Nakase also made a change in the starting lineup, Hayes and Kaila Charles for Kayla Thornton and Cecilia Zandalasini. While the Valkyries got off to a slow start again in the early afternoon tipoff with the Atlanta Hawks playing their home opener at night, when Thornton and Zandalasini entered the game they paid immediate dividends. The two helped a key first-quarter run that gave Golden State its first lead since the third quarter of Game 2. Atlanta got within 24-20 on Reese’s basket — her lone one of the first half — but the Valkyries responded with an 18-6 run to close the half. The 42-26 deficit at the break was the largest that the Dream had faced all playoffs. Atlanta had dominated the third quarter in the WNBA Finals, outscoring Golden State 60-35 in the first three games. The Valkyries wouldn’t let them do that in Game 4.

articles.title: Preocupa el estado de salud de Ric Flair tras desplomarse en mitad de la calle
articles.standfirst: El mítico luchador había anunciado poco antes que tenía un coágulo de sangre en una pierna
articles.summary: El mítico luchador había anunciado poco antes que tenía un coágulo de sangre en una pierna
articles.body: La leyenda de la lucha libre Ric Flair fue trasladado ayer de urgencia a un hospital de Tampa (Florida) después de sufrir una fuerte caída cuando salió de un restaurante. Según informó el portal TMZ, el carismático wrestler de 77 años se desplomó y como consecuencia sufrió cortes en la cabeza y en la zona alrededor del ojo. El incidente ocurrió apenas horas después de que Flair revelara que está lidiando con un coágulo de sangre en una pierna que le impedía realizar un viaje a un evento con fans en Seattle. Según TMZ, el luchador se encontraba en el restaurante Wagamama de Tampa, se levantó de la barra dejando allí su teléfono y su bebida, y cruzó la calle. Ya en el exterior, cayó de forma repentina y se golpeó la cabeza. El mismo viernes, Flair explicó en sus cuentas de redes sociales: “Lamentablemente, tengo un coágulo sanguíneo en la pierna y mis médicos han limitado mis desplazamientos a un máximo de 3 o 4 horas. Seattle queda fuera de ese rango y, por mucho que me pese, debo priorizar mi salud y mi recuperación […] Tengo programada una intervención para tratar la vena afectada; mis médicos esperan que, tras el procedimiento, pueda volver a realizar viajes más largos”. Horas después de su caída, ‘The Nature Boy’ compartió una foto desde el hospital con un mensaje para sus seguidores: “¡Gracias a todos por los mensajes y oraciones! Les responderé a cada uno individualmente a medida que me fortalezca. Gracias a todo el personal y médicos del Tampa General Hospital que me soportaron hasta las 4:30 de la mañana. Los aprecio a todos y gracias por todo lo que hicieron por mí. En este momento estoy enfocado en mi sanación y recuperación. ¡Estaré bien!”. Flair no detalló si su caída fue consecuencia del coágulo, aunque a priori parece la causa.

articles.title: Quinn Hughes Teases New Wild Contract Amid NHL Rumors After Connor Hellebuyck Devils Trade
articles.summary: Star defenseman Quinn Hughes said he might sign a contract extension with the Minnesota Wild "soon" rather than test free agency and gain the opportunity to join his brothers and Team USA teammate Connor Hellebuyck on the New Jersey Devils.
articles.body:
Star defenseman Quinn Hughes said he might sign a contract extension with the Minnesota Wild "soon" rather than test free agency and gain the opportunity to join his brothers and Team USA teammate Connor Hellebuyck on the New Jersey Devils.

"I'm where I've always been, and I'm excited right now, and my two feet are planted here in Minnesota," Hughes told reporters Saturday when asked about his mindset regarding contract negotiations. "Something could happen soon, I'm not really too sure."

Hughes added part of his excitement hinges on the opportunity to play with a defensive core starring Jared Spurgeon, Jonas Brodin and Brock Faber while Kirill Kaprizov, Matt Boldy and Joel Eriksson Ek lead the Wild's offense.

"I'm really enjoying playing here, and I love playing with— you see Brod, Spurge, and when Brock Faber comes back, there's a lot of things that are set up nicely for me to have success individually," Hughes said.

Hughes concluded, "I would think we have a chance to win this year. And then, you see when [head coach John Hynes] and [associate coach Jack Capuano] load us up with Kirill and Boldy and Ek— that's probably the most fun hockey I've ever played, just playing with those guys... I'm really enjoying it right now, and just taking my time, and we'll see where it goes. But wouldn't be surprised if something happens soon."

Hughes, who was traded from the Vancouver Canucks to the Wild last December, is in the final season of his $7.85 million AAV contract.

Questions about his future escalated after the Devils acquired Hellebuyck, a three-time Vezina Trophy winner, from the Winnipeg Jets.

The Devils are off to a 6-4-0 start to the season with Jack Hughes and Luke Hughes on the roster.

Adding Hellebuyck could make New Jersey an even more appealing destination as a contender, although the Devils would have to clear out cap space in order to fit what is likely to be a significant raise for Hughes under the cap.

Hughes said Saturday he hadn't spoken with his brothers "too much yet" about the trade for Hellebuyck.

"I know Helly. I know what Jack feels about him. He lives eight houses down from us in Michigan, skates with us in the summer, and then obviously won gold with him," Hughes said. "I'm sure he's happy, and this is what he wanted, so for me, just being his friend, happy for him."

Hellebuyck, who hasn't played in an NHL game since last April, will continue preparing for his Devils debut while the Wild continue extension talks with Hughes.

The Colorado Avalanche's Cale Makar set a defensive record by signing a deal worth more than $20 million per year in August. Whatever contract Hughes signs next could once more reset the market for a blueliner.

articles.title: Indiana outlasts Michigan in overtime for first win at Big House since 1967
articles.summary: Josh Hoover's overtime touchdown run lifted No. 6 Indiana football past Michigan at the Big House for the first time since 1967 under Curt Cignetti.
articles.body: There have been few reasons to celebrate in Ann Arbor over the three seasons since Michigan won the College Football Playoff national championship. On Saturday, the Wolverines’ misery continued as they failed to reach the end zone when they needed it most and suffered their third loss of the season, a 13-6 overtime defeat to defending national champion Indiana. Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover scored on a 4-yard touchdown run in overtime, then the Hoosiers’ defense stopped Michigan on its ensuing possession to secure a 13-6 victory. The win also prevented Indiana from suffering its first two-game losing streak in three years under coach Curt Cignetti and marked the Hoosiers’ first victory at Michigan Stadium since 1967. OLE MISS AND TEXAS COLLIDE IN MASSIVE COLLEGE FOOTBALL SHOWDOWN WITH ARCH MANNING'S SEASON AT STAKE Tommy Carr started at quarterback for the Wolverines, while Bryce Underwood sat out. However, Carr, a freshman, didn’t fare as well as he did last week, when he came off the bench to help Michigan defeat Penn State. Carr lost a fumble on an ill-advised pitch in the first quarter and was picked off in the second half. He took sacks in the second and third quarters that led to missed field goals, including a 32-yard kick after advancing to the Indiana 1. articles.title: Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley praise Cam Jurgens ahead of Ravens debut
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley recently praised Cam Jurgens' football intelligence, preparation and quick adjustment to the Ravens' offense.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens made a significant investment in their offensive line by acquiring Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles . Early reviews from the quarterback room suggest he is already making a strong impression.

Jurgens arrived in Baltimore while recovering from a concussion , giving him an unusual start with a new team, offense, and group of teammates. Despite those circumstances, he has worked to get up to speed with offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's system while building chemistry with the quarterbacks.

Both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley have noticed how quickly the new center has picked things up, particularly in communication and understanding the offense. Jackson, speaking with the media on Friday, said he was especially impressed by how quickly Jurgens began making calls on the field and expressed excitement about playing alongside him.

"[Cam Jurgens is] awesome, man. That guy's smart. He's calling out stuff already. I was shocked. I'm like, damn, he's a pro. I'm looking forward to playing with Cam. It's going to be great. He's going to be great for us. [He's a] great addition to the squad for sure."

Jackson's assessment is significant, given the importance of communication between a quarterback and his center. Jurgens must learn the terminology and responsibilities of a new offense while helping coordinate front-side protection, and his ability to make calls confidently could help the Ravens establish greater consistency along the offensive line.

Tyler Huntley sees Jurgens putting in the extra work

Huntley has also seen his new teammate's preparation firsthand, including the work Jurgens puts in when he's not taking snaps. Huntley also spoke with media members , and he praised Jurgens' willingness to keep asking questions and working through assignments, rather than limiting his attention to the reps he gets on the field. He also emphasized how well Jurgens has handled his responsibilities when he gets another opportunity to work with the offense.

"[Cam Jurgens] is doing a great job. Even when he's not in, or when he just took his reps that day, he's been in the back asking what the plays are, working through his calls. When he gets back in, he's been amazing... He's been doing a great job. He's been doing great, going out there every single play that he's out there [and] making his calls. He's doing great"

Jurgens could bring stability to Baltimore's offensive line

The Ravens have dealt with considerable turnover along the interior of their offensive line, making Jurgens' arrival particularly important. His ability to communicate protections and build chemistry with the quarterbacks could help Baltimore improve its execution as the offense works to become more consistent.

Jurgens also brings experience at center, a position that requires more than winning individual blocking assignments. He must help identify defensive looks, communicate adjustments, and ensure the players around him understand their responsibilities before the snap.

The early praise from Jackson and Huntley suggests Jurgens is taking those responsibilities seriously. The next step is translating that preparation into game-day performance, starting with Baltimore's matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals .

If Jurgens can turn his quick grasp of the offense into dependable communication and stronger execution up front, the Ravens could benefit from his presence well beyond his individual performance at center.
